english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the person concerned in respect of **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), a ship in respect of which there was a contravention of regulation 34-1 of Chapter V of the Annex to the SOLAS convention in that **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 20 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002.

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 22 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged under these Regulations to show that he took all reasonable steps to avoid the commission of the offence.
(ii) Paragraph 20 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 provides that an offence under this regulation shall be an offence by the person concerned.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
